name: index_rebalance_flow_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-3
thesis: NSE announces NIFTY 50 / NIFTY Next 50 index rebalances semi-annually (March and September), with the effective date 2-3 weeks after announcement. Stocks being ADDED to the index experience sustained buying pressure from passive funds and ETFs (NIFTY BeES, SBI NIFTY ETF, etc.) that must buy before the effective date. Stocks being REMOVED face selling pressure. The rebalance-driven flow is predictable because: (1) passive fund AUM in India has grown to ₹7+ lakh crore, (2) the buying/selling is mandatory and concentrated in the week before the effective date, (3) the flow size relative to ADV can be 5-20% for NIFTY Next 50 additions. On the EFFECTIVE DATE itself, the final adjustment happens in the closing auction, but intraday we can capture the drift as passive funds execute throughout the day.
universe: Stocks being added/removed from NIFTY 50, NIFTY Next 50, NIFTY 100
stock_filter: Stocks announced for addition/removal, ADV > ₹15 crore

other: passive fund AUM tracking NIFTY indices
estimated shares to be bought/sold by passive funds

indicators.name: estimated_passive_demand
indicators.formula: total_passive_aum * new_index_weight / stock_price (shares to be bought by passives)

conditions: stock is being ADDED to index
rebalance_countdown <= 5 (within 5 trading days of effective date)
demand_to_adv > 10 (meaningful passive demand relative to daily volume)
close > VWAP (passive buying already pushing price up)
long.confirmation: volume_today > 1.3 * ADV_20 (passive flow visibly increasing volume)

conditions: stock is being REMOVED from index
close < VWAP (passive selling pushing price down)

exit.target: 30 bps from entry (capturing a slice of the multi-day drift)
exit.time_stop: exit by 15:15 IST (intraday only, no overnight hold)

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX < 25 (market stress may overwhelm rebalance flow)
filters.time_filter: no entries after 14:00 (too close to EOD flatten)
filters.trend_filter: prefer rebalance direction aligned with NIFTY 50 direction
filters.event_filter: skip if stock has earnings/corporate action during rebalance window
other_filters: skip stocks with demand_to_adv < 10 (passive flow too small to move price)

edge.edge_decay_risk: Low — passive fund growth in India is accelerating, making rebalance flows larger over time. The edge may actually INCREASE as passive AUM grows. However, more front-runners will also enter, compressing returns.

weaknesses: Only 4-6 stocks are added/removed per semi-annual rebalance. The strategy generates trades on only ~10 days per year (5 days before each rebalance).
Index rebalance front-running is increasingly crowded. Hedge funds and prop desks buy additions weeks before the effective date, reducing the residual edge for last-week entries.
Passive fund managers may not execute VWAP — some use closing auction, some spread over multiple days. Our estimate of daily flow may be wrong.
prior_art: Harris & Gurel (1986) 'Price and Volume Effects Associated with Changes in the S&P 500'. Chen, Noronha & Singal (2004) 'The Price Response to S&P 500 Index Additions and Deletions'. In India, Chakrabarti et al. (2005) study index effect in emerging markets. Petajisto (2011) estimates cost of index rebalancing.
notes: Monitor NSE index advisory committee announcements (typically 4 weeks before effective date). Start tracking the announced additions/deletions immediately. The intraday component captures only a fraction of the total rebalance effect — most of the alpha is in the multi-day drift, which requires overnight positions (out of scope for this intraday-only constraint).
